A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Juno is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **Juno-60** was made by **Roland** and came out in **September 1982**; production ended in February 1984 (Wikipedia, "Roland Juno-60").
- It has **six voices** and **56 patch memories** (Juno-60 manual, p. 2). The **Juno-106** that followed has 128 patches and MIDI (Juno-106 manual, p. 1).
- Wikipedia says it "had an immediate impact in 1980s pop music".

## Its sound

- Each voice has **one oscillator** (a DCO), with saw, pulse, a **sub-oscillator** an octave down and noise (Juno-60 manual, pp. 12-13).
- **PWM**: the pulse wave's width can move with the LFO, which sounds like a group of strings (manual, pp. 12-13).
- The built-in **chorus** (I or II) makes one oscillator sound wide and thick (manual, p. 22). It became its signature sound (Wikipedia).
- A **high-pass filter** and a low-pass filter (manual, p. 14).

## Guided tour

Each step loads a worked example from the compare page and changes one thing.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="juno-bass" data-set="{&quot;sub&quot;:false}"><p><b>Saw only.</b> One sawtooth oscillator. Listen: a simple bass.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="juno-bass"><p><b>Add the sub-oscillator.</b> The <b>Sub osc</b> adds a square wave one octave down. Listen: much fuller and deeper.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="juno-strings" data-set="{&quot;chorus&quot;:&quot;off&quot;,&quot;pwm&quot;:0,&quot;pwmMode&quot;:&quot;man&quot;}"><p><b>A plain pulse pad.</b> Pulse wave, chorus off, no PWM. Listen: thin and still.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="juno-strings" data-set="{&quot;chorus&quot;:&quot;off&quot;}"><p><b>PWM by the LFO.</b> The pulse width now moves with the LFO. Listen for a slow shimmer.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="juno-strings" data-set="{&quot;chorus&quot;:&quot;I&quot;}"><p><b>Chorus I.</b> Listen: the sound spreads out and gets wider.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="juno-strings"><p><b>Chorus II.</b> The faster, deeper chorus. Listen: the classic thick Juno pad.</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Roland Juno-60":

- a-ha, "Take On Me"
- George Michael, "A Different Corner"
- Cyndi Lauper, "Time After Time"

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How many oscillators does each Juno voice have?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li><li>Three</li><li>Six</li></ul><p class="ik-why">One DCO, plus a sub-oscillator.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does the chorus do to the sound?</b></p><ul><li>Makes it wider and thicker</li><li>Makes it one note at a time</li><li>Adds drums</li><li>Turns it off</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Steps 5 and 6.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>The sub-oscillator plays…</b></p><ul><li>One octave below</li><li>One octave above</li><li>A fifth above</li><li>Only noise</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 2.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="2"><p><b>How many voices does the Juno-60 have?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Five</li><li>Six</li><li>Sixteen</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 2.</p></div>
```

::: {.works-cited}
**For students**

Roland. *Juno-60 Owner's Manual*. Roland Corporation, Apr. 1983, [soundprogramming.net/manuals/Roland_Juno-60_Manual.pdf](https://soundprogramming.net/manuals/Roland_Juno-60_Manual.pdf). Six voices and 56 patches (p. 2); DCO with no portamento, PWM, sub-oscillator, noise (pp. 12-13); HPF and VCF (p. 14); VCA and envelope (p. 16); LFO with delay (p. 17); chorus I and II (p. 22); specifications (p. 32). A scan, read by OCR. Faithful panel (panels/juno.js): positions measured off the fold-out panel drawing, PDF p. 5.

**For teachers**

Roland. *Juno-106 Owner's Manual*. Roland Corporation, [soundprogramming.net/manuals/Roland_Juno-106_Manual.pdf](https://soundprogramming.net/manuals/Roland_Juno-106_Manual.pdf). 128 patches, portamento and MIDI (p. 1); the HPF at 0 boosts the bass (p. 18); portamento (p. 23); chorus I and II not at the same time (p. 29). A scan, read by OCR.

"Roland Juno-60." *Wikipedia*, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Juno-60](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Juno-60). A 24 dB-per-octave resonant low-pass and a non-resonant high-pass filter; the chorus buttons' rates of 0.4 and 0.6 Hz.
:::
